title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with synthetic media. An AI-generated video presented a well-known financial sector personality as the face of an investment offering significant returns, and the victim's decision to invest rested on that apparent endorsement. The failure sits at the very front of the deployment, in the advertising and trust-building stage, before any real financial service existed to be checked.

Nothing in the chain required the fraudsters to defeat a technical control, because there was no control at the point of contact. Catching it would have taken confirming that the person shown had actually endorsed the investment, and confirming that the provider was authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. The later steps, the WhatsApp contact, the requests for more money, the opening of several accounts and the granting of remote access, are where the loss was escalated rather than where it began.

The reporting does not establish which celebrity was depicted, and the PSNI did not confirm one. BBC News NI has seen separate scams using other named financial figures, which is not a finding that any of them were involved in this one. The police description of a sophisticated and substantial fraud is an investigative statement, not a court finding.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in Ards and north Down lost £250,000 after an AI-generated video scam. The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the victim saw an advert that appeared to feature a well-known financial sector personality and promoted an investment with significant returns. After a small investment, the victim was contacted on WhatsApp and urged to pay more. The fraudsters had the victim open several accounts and gave themselves remote access to their computer, saying they were helping with the investment.

Police called it a sophisticated and substantial fraud. The victim was encouraged to borrow money, and the funds went to accounts controlled by criminals. The PSNI did not confirm which celebrity was used, though BBC News NI has seen scams using financial experts Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett. Superintendent Joanne Gibson of the Scamwise Partnership urged people to stop and check financial activity and for families to talk about fraud. Police advised people to independently verify who they are dealing with and to check that providers are authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
